Sharma and Parton (2007) DBH–height models for Ontario boreal tree species

Source: R/hd_sharmaparton2007.R
hd_sharmaparton2007.Rd

Vectorized implementation of the population-level individual-tree height–diameter models of Sharma and Parton (2007) for boreal tree species in northern Ontario. Predicts total tree height (m) from DBH (cm) and three stand-level predictors: dominant stand height, basal area and stand density.

Usage

hd_sharmaparton2007(DBH, species, HDOM, BA, TPH, keep_model_id = FALSE)

Arguments

DBH

Numeric vector. Tree level. Diameter at breast height (1.3 m above ground), in cm. Must be >= 0.

species

Character vector. Tree level. NFI species codes (e.g. "PICE.MAR"; compact "PICEMAR" is accepted).

HDOM

Numeric vector. Plot level. Dominant stand height (m): the "mean height of sampled dominant and codominant trees in a plot, irrespective of species" (source "SHT", p. 190). Must be > 0.

BA

Numeric vector. Plot level. Total stand basal area (m²/ha) of all trees in the plot (source "BA/ha", p. 188 and p. 190). The source does not state a minimum DBH for this total. Must be > 0.

TPH

Numeric vector. Plot level. Stand density (stems/ha), "calculated from the trees with DBH greater than or equal to 2.5 cm" (source "N/ha", p. 188). Must be > 0.

keep_model_id

Logical. If TRUE, add column model_id ("sharmaparton2007").

Value

A tibble with column height (m) and, if keep_model_id = TRUE, model_id.

Details

Model scope (species coverage): balsam fir (ABIE.BAL), balsam poplar (POPU.BAL), black spruce (PICE.MAR), jack pine (PINU.BAN), red pine (PINU.RES), trembling aspen (POPU.TRE), white birch (BETU.PAP) and white spruce (PICE.GLA). Fitted to permanent growth study plots in northern Ontario; tree origin (natural or planted) was recorded (p. 188), but the source does not state whether planted trees were excluded.

Model form (eqs. 6 and 8, p. 190 and p. 192): $$H = 1.3 + \theta \, HDOM^{\delta} [1 - \exp(-\beta (TPH / BA)^{\phi} DBH)]^{\gamma}.$$

Height convention: total tree height; DBH measured at 1.3 m, so predicted height tends to 1.3 m as DBH tends to 0.

Population-level prediction: coefficients are the fixed effects of the mixed-effects fit (Method 2, Table 6, p. 195), evaluated with the plot-level random effect on the asymptote set to zero (\(u = 0\)). This gives the curve of a "typical" plot with the supplied stand characteristics, as shown in Fig. 2 of the source. Plot-specific calibration with measured heights (eq. 7) is not implemented.

Rows with NA in any input return NA height. Inputs outside the range of the fitting data (per-species DBH, Table 1; pooled plot BA, TPH and HDOM ranges, p. 188) are computed and reported in a single warning.

References

Sharma, M., and Parton, J. (2007). Height–diameter equations for boreal tree species in Ontario using a mixed-effects modeling approach. Forest Ecology and Management, 249(3), 187–198. doi:10.1016/j.foreco.2007.05.006

See also

hd_model_registry(), get_hd_model_info()

Examples

hd_sharmaparton2007(
  DBH = c(10, 20, 30),
  species = c("PICE.MAR", "PINU.BAN", "POPU.TRE"),
  HDOM = 20, BA = 25, TPH = 2500
)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 1
#>   height
#>    <dbl>
#> 1   11.9
#> 2   20.6
#> 3   22.3

# Inside dplyr::mutate() with tree and plot data
trees <- data.frame(
  DBH = c(12, 25, 18),
  species = c("ABIE.BAL", "PICE.GLA", "BETU.PAP"),
  HDOM = c(16, 16, 22), BA = c(30, 30, 18), TPH = c(3000, 3000, 1200)
)
dplyr::mutate(trees, hd_sharmaparton2007(DBH, species, HDOM, BA, TPH))
#>   DBH  species HDOM BA  TPH   height
#> 1  12 ABIE.BAL   16 30 3000 11.08370
#> 2  25 PICE.GLA   16 30 3000 16.97600
#> 3  18 BETU.PAP   22 18 1200 18.25566
